newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Steel cuts losses, sees '97 profit.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Steel cuts losses, sees '97 profit.

text.p: Swiss Steel AG, a new steel company created by the partial merger of operations of Von Moos Holding and Von Roll, reduced its first half loss to 6.1 million Swiss francs from 11.6 million and expects to be able to report a slight net profit for 1997.

Swiss Steel said in a statement that net sales in the first six months rose to 379.4 million francs from 278.9 million and the operating loss fell to 0.5 million from 10.1 million, achiving the company's targets. Based on the first six months, Swiss Steel said it was very confident that it would be able to more than halve the ordinary loss in 1997 to around 20 million francs.
Due to provisions created in 1996, the company also assumes it can report a slight net profit for the full year.
